chapter: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
title: Woodborn gig in the Catskills (second pass)
summary: Repeat account of being called with Fathead Lawrence to replace Erskine Hawkins's rhythm section.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Okay, so you made the trip to New York with Tiny Bradshaw and then back to Philly and that was '34, then what happened?
'34. The dates are kind of running into one another because when I left Les Robinson at the Club Harlem, I came to the Catskills.
" You went to the Catskill mountains?
How did you happen to go up there?
I got a wire, got a call.
The rhythm section of the Erskine Hawkins band had been off, and they were working here.
Lou _______ Morgan who is still around and I forget the bass player's name, if I can think of it -- Lee, I don't know.

And the drummer, and Erskine has a gig and so they have to come back and they need a replacement so Fathead Lawrence, I'm going to have to look that up too, a baritone player, hell of a baritone player, played without a strap --
Must have had some strong hands.
He and I were called from Philadelphia to make the gig so we went to Woodborn and the mountains wasn't too populated at that time so the gig closed before Labor Day.
And we came back to New York, he was from Hampton, Virginia and he went to Virginia and I came to New York.
Lawrence. And that's how I stayed in New York.
